title: Knowing When Not to Reach for AI
objective: Identify a real, upcoming piece of work where you deliberately do not use AI-generated code because it is an irreversible operation, security-sensitive code, or a requirement that is still genuinely unclear, and produce a written case for that decision plus the work completed without it.
whyThisMatters: The AI-native skill this curriculum is built around is not 'always use AI' — it is judgment about when the risk of an unverified or premature suggestion outweighs the speed gain.
evidence: A decision memo, written and committed before starting the work, naming the specific risk and why it justified not using AI generation for this piece
Git history or a work log showing incremental progress on the withheld work without AI-generated implementation code
A note on where AI was still used for the task, if at all, distinguished clearly from what was deliberately withheld
A reflection on what would have had to be true for the decision to go the other way
acceptanceCriteria: The decision memo is committed before the implementation work it concerns.
The named risk is one of: an irreversible operation, security-sensitive code, or an explicitly unclear requirement, and the memo explains which and why.
No AI-generated implementation code appears in the submitted work for the withheld part, per the disclosure entry.
The reflection names a concrete condition, not a vague hedge, under which the decision would have been different.
